To: rafael_mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@medicahealth.com>
Subject: Private deployment — BYOK controls & operator access (initial asks)

Rafael,

Thanks again for the product walkthrough last week — Medica is excited about Redwood's private deployment option. Before we proceed to procurement we need to iron out a few items for our security team so purchasing can move forward: 

- BYOK scope: we require that tenant CMKs remain under our KMS and that Redwood cannot export key material. Need language around customer-controlled key lifecycle and key-wrapping operations.
- Operator access: we need explicit limits on what Redwood engineers can access for on-prem vs VPC deployments (telemetry, logs, model artifacts, KV cache).
- Subprocessors: please share your current subproc list and commit to 30 days notice prior to adding a subprocessor with access to customer ciphertext or metadata.
- International transfers: Medica processes EU patient metadata; if any operator support crosses borders we must ensure SCCs or alternative transfer mechanisms are in place.

Can you share a DPA addendum or sample language? We can route it to our legal/security teams after an initial pass.

Best,
Sanjay
Director, Security & Privacy
Medica Health

Sanjay — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a DPA addendum redline that addresses the BYOK lifecycle, operator roles, and a proposed subprocessors notice clause. High-level notes: 

- BYOK: we can support a customer-controlled KMS where Redwood only holds wrapped keys and performs cryptographic operations with no plaintext export. We'll flag a carve-out for emergency break-glass operator actions (audit-only; requires 2-person approval + customer OOB consent).
- Operator access: propose an explicit "operator entitlements" table in the addendum (read-only traces, aggregated telemetry) and deny access to model artifacts and raw customer inputs unless mutually agreed and logged.
- Subprocessors: current list attached. Redwood proposes 45-day notice and a right-to-review; if Medica requires 30-day notice we can take that to Legal for discussion.
- Transfers: we'll include SCC reference and the option to restrict support to US/EU-only operator staff for this account.

Looping in Lauren (Enterprise Legal) to confirm redline and next steps. If this looks directionally correct, I'll share with our security/compliance owners (Monica + Karthik) for technical confirmation.

Regards,
Rafael Mendes
Sr. Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference

- Break-glass: standard carve with documented approvals sounds OK but legal wants to add a limited scope + 30-day post-incident reporting requirement.
- Subprocessors notice: we prefer 45 days to be able to manage vendor changes internally, but operationally 30 days is defensible for enterprise customers — suggest we offer 30 days for Medica as a concession in exchange for a 12-month fixed term on Dedicated capacity.
- Transfers/SCCs: legal will not accept ad-hoc cross-border operator access without SCCs and documented lawful basis.

Monica/karthik: please confirm technical feasibility of the operator-entitlements table and the break-glass approval flow (2-person approval + customer OOB consent).

Subject: Re: Private deployment — BYOK controls & operator access (technical confirmation)

Lauren/ Rafael — brief technical confirmations below: 

- BYOK: Supported. For VPC/on-prem we operate with wrapped-key models where the CMK is never exported. We can add an auditable HSM-backed unwrap operation that increments an incident ledger. Cryptographic primitives and key-wrapping are compatible with all major KMS (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, self-hosted HSM).
- Break-glass: feasible but requires an ops runbook: 2-person approval (Senior Ops + Security on call) + recorded WebRTC OOB consent from the customer admin. All actions generate immutable telemetry and a signed incident package for customer review.
- Operator-entitlements table: we propose these rows — "Support session (live, read-only telemetry)", "Log retrieval (redacted) limited to last 30 days", "No model artifact access", "No raw customer inputs except with explicit consent".
- Subprocessor notice: we can automate notifications; 30-day notice is fine for Medica if Legal accepts an exception to standard 45-day practice.

I'll attach a short ops runbook and the entitlements table to the next email.

Monica Patel
Head of Security Engineering — Redwood Inference

Attachment: ops-runbook-byok-breakglass.pdf

Key commercial/contract items for your team to review: 
- Notice window: Redwood can accept 30-day notice to Medica for subprocessors tied to this account in exchange for a 12-month Dedicated commitment (we'll reference the purchase order). If Medica prefers no commitment, we revert to standard 45-day vendor change notice.
- Break-glass: technical controls and audit artifacts included. We ask for a short bilateral SLA addendum covering response windows for on-call operator actions.
- Geo-limited support: we can scope operator access to US/EU-only staff for your account and reference SCCs in the addendum.

Next steps I propose: 
1) Medica legal reviews the attached redline and returns comments to this thread (or mark up the doc).
2) We run a 30-minute technical call with Monica + Karthik to walk through the entitlements table and the runbook.
3) Commercial: confirm if Medica is willing to commit to a 12-month Dedicated reservation (will change subprocessors notice window).

If that works I'll initiate the technical call invite for early next week.

Thanks,
